sections.label: Mediation and Civil Law Bills
sections.summary: Two Bills are tabled in 2017 to grow dispute resolution work in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In the next decade, when trust commands an even higher premium, Singapore is well poised to achieve even more.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We are tabling two Bills today − the Mediation Bill and the Civil Law (Amendment) Bill − as part of a number of moves that we will make in 2017 to grow dispute resolution work in Singapore to the next level.

sections.label: SIMC case filings
sections.summary: By end 2016 SIMC attracted case filings from over 20 jurisdictions, with sums in dispute from S$0.5 million to over S$600 million.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: SIMC has, as of end 2016, successfully attracted case filings from parties from more than 20 different jurisdictions and a wide range of industries and sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The sums in dispute ranged from S$0.5 million to more than S$600 million.

sections.label: SIMI credentialing and partner schemes
sections.summary: SIMI maintains a four-tiered credentialing scheme for 116 mediators and a three-tiered partner scheme for two organisations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: As a professional standards body for mediation, SIMI has successfully implemented and maintains a four-tiered credentialing scheme for 116 − and growing − local and international mediators, and a three-tiered partner scheme for two − soon to be seven − organisations offering mediation services and/or training.

sections.label: Expedited enforcement of settlement agreements
sections.summary: The Bill provides an additional expedited way for parties to ensure a settlement agreement is enforceable.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The Bill, therefore, provides an additional expedited way for parties to ensure that the settlement agreement is enforceable.

sections.label: Requirements for settlement agreements
sections.summary: The settlement agreement must be in writing and the mediation administered by a designated provider or conducted by a certified mediator.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The settlement agreement must be in writing, and the mediation administered by a designated mediation service provider, or conducted by a certified mediator.

sections.label: Confidentiality of mediation communications
sections.summary: Except in narrow circumstances, mediation communications cannot be disclosed to third parties or admitted as evidence in Court or arbitral proceedings.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The Bill makes clear that except under narrow circumstances set out under the Bill, communications made in a mediation cannot be disclosed to third parties to the mediation and cannot be admitted in Court or arbitral proceedings as evidence.

sections.label: Statutory basis to stay proceedings
sections.summary: The Bill gives parties to a mediation agreement a statutory basis to apply to Court to stay ongoing proceedings on the same dispute.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The Bill will provide parties to a mediation agreement with a specific statutory basis to apply to Court to stay any ongoing Court proceedings in relation to the same dispute.

sections.label: Mediation Bill framework in Singapore
sections.summary: The Mediation Bill introduces a coherent mediation framework covering aspects such as confidentiality and enforceability of mediated settlement agreements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The Mediation Bill serves to introduce a coherent mediation framework in Singapore on various aspects of mediation currently dealt with by agreement between parties to mediation, such as issues of confidentiality and enforceability of mediated settlement agreements.

sections.label: Mediation before litigation and limitation period
sections.summary: The Member asks whether the Bill aims to promote mediation as mainstream dispute resolution and whether it can provide suspension or extension of the limitation period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Could the Senior Minister of State kindly clarify if the policy intention behind the Mediation Bill vis a vis litigation in the Courts is to promote mediation as a mainstream form of dispute resolution mechanism rather than an alternative dispute resolution, that is, to encourage parties, especially commercial parties, to turn to pre-action mediation to resolve their disputes before resorting to litigation or arbitration?

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: If so, I wonder if the Mediation Bill can be strengthened even further to encourage parties to refer their dispute to mediation before litigating by providing for a suspension or extension of the limitation period for instituting litigation or arbitration of a case that is being mediated.

sections.label: Legal aid extended to mediation
sections.summary: The Member asks whether legal aid may be extended to cover mediation, since pre-action mediation can save cost and time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Since costs of legally aided persons are borne by the state and it is plainly obvious that pre-action mediation can result in significant savings of cost and time, I wonder if legal aid may be extended to cover mediation as well.

sections.label: Clause 8 stay and interim orders
sections.summary: Clause 8 enables parties to a mediation agreement to apply to Court for a stay of proceedings and for interim or supplementary orders.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Clause 8, for example, enables parties to a mediation agreement to apply to Court for a stay of proceedings and for the Court to make interim or supplementary orders to preserve the parties' rights as long as the Court proceedings relate to the subject of the mediation agreement.

sections.label: Mediated settlement recorded as Court order
sections.summary: A new clause allows parties to consensually apply to Court for a record of the mediated settlement as an enforceable order of Court.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: That is, that mediated settlements are only contractually enforceable between parties.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This new clause allows parties to consensually apply to Court for a record of the mediated settlement as an order of Court which can be enforced in the same manner as a Court judgment would.

sections.label: Mediation confidentiality duty and exceptions
sections.summary: The Bill imposes a general duty of confidentiality over all mediation communications, with defined carve-outs and exceptions permitting disclosure in certain circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Bill prescribes a general duty of confidentiality over all mediation communications with defined crave-outs and exceptions under which disclosure may take place in certain circumstances.

sections.label: Exclusion of written law mediations
sections.summary: Clause 6(2)(a) states the Act does not apply to mediation or conciliation conducted under or provided by any written law.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Clause 6(2)(a) states that "this Act does not apply to, or in relation to any mediation or conciliation proceeding, process, scheme or framework conducted under, or provided by or under, any written law".

sections.label: Enforcement of mediated settlement agreements
sections.summary: Clause 12 lets a settlement agreement be enforced like a Court order where parties agree, instead of only as a contractual claim.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Clause 12 of the Bill provides the welcome ability for a settlement agreement to have the potential to be enforced in the same manner as a Court order where parties agree.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Currently, a settlement agreement is purely contractual, requiring further action to enforce the bite of the settlement agreement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Without this amendment, a party has to go through the onerous steps of enforcing the agreement as a contractual claim or apply to Court for a consent order.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This Bill remedies this deficiency and enhances the attractiveness of mediation as a choice alternative dispute resolution with finality and expediency where the parties decide to exercise this right.

sections.label: Foreign mediators and foreign-qualified counsel
sections.summary: The Legal Profession Act amendment clarifies that foreign mediators and foreign-qualified counsel participating in such mediations do not practise Singapore law unauthorised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The amendment to the Legal Profession Act makes clear that participation by foreign mediators and foreign-qualified counsel in such mediation sessions will not amount to unauthorised practice of Singapore law.

sections.label: Recording mediated settlement as Court order
sections.summary: Clause 12 allows a mediated settlement agreement to be recorded as an order of Court with parties' consent, subject to qualifying factors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Clause 12 of the Mediation Bill allows the recording of a mediated settlement agreement as an order of Court with parties' consent where the mediation is administered by a designated mediation service provider or conducted by a certified mediator and subject to other qualifying factors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: This facilitates the ease of enforcement of the mediation settlement agreement as parties currently have to commence legal proceedings to enforce the settlement agreement.

sections.label: Justifications for regulating mediators
sections.summary: Four justifications support regulating mediators: protecting the public, informing the public, improving mediator ability, and enhancing professional credibility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Four justifications to support regulating mediators include: (a) protecting the public from problematic mediators; (b) providing information to the public about mediators; (c) improving mediator ability and capabilities; and (d) enhancing the credibility of the profession.

sections.label: Number of appointed service providers
sections.summary: The passage asks the Minister for clarification on how many service providers, including foreign ones, will be appointed.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: I just have a few clarifications for the Minister.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: And how many service providers are we looking at appointing further and, especially, foreign ones as well?

sections.label: Mediator registration and training requirements
sections.summary: The passage asks about the registration and training requirements of mediators from the appointed service providers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: What about the registration and training requirements of the mediators from the appointed service providers?

sections.label: Specialist mediators and resource list
sections.summary: The passage asks whether specialist mediators will be considered and whether a list of resource mediators will be formalised.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Experience and ability to engage people becomes important.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Therefore, will there also be some kind of consideration for specialist mediators?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Will we be planning to have this more formalised and made available or, perhaps, have a list of resource mediators who can be called upon for such relevant cases?

sections.label: Mediation as complementary dispute resolution
sections.summary: The passage states mediation is complementary to litigation and arbitration and that the government is committed to mediation for amicable, cost-effective dispute settlement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, in that context, mediation is complementary to litigation and arbitration and it is important to recognise that there are unique circumstances behind individual disputes, and having alternative dispute resolution mechanisms will enable the parties to find the right solution to address their issues.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We are committed to mediation as a means for parties to settle disputes amicably and in a cost-effective way.

sections.label: Legal aid covering mediations
sections.summary: The passage clarifies that legal aid covers mediations conducted as part of resolving disputes between parties.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The Member's second set of suggestions related to the provision of legal aid.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: I should clarify that legal aid does, in fact, cover mediations which are conducted as part of the process of resolving the dispute between parties.

sections.label: Bill does not regulate mediation
sections.summary: The passage states the Bill does not itself regulate the provision of mediation services or accreditation of mediators.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The Bill does not itself regulate the provision of mediation services or accreditation of mediators.

sections.label: SIMI as mediation standards body
sections.summary: SIMI was established as the premier independent professional standards body to promote mediation and set high competency standards.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: To that end, we have established SIMI as the premier independent professional standards body, to promote mediation and set high competency standards in mediation practice.

sections.label: Designated provider and certified mediator
sections.summary: The designated mediation service provider and certified mediator serve a limited purpose as prerequisites for enforcing a mediated settlement agreement as a Court order.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The "designated mediation service provider" and "certified mediator" contained in the Bill serve a limited purpose.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Specifically, in order for parties to make use of the provision to enable the enforcement of a mediated settlement agreement recorded as a Court order in clause 12 of the Bill, it is a pre-requisite that the mediation in question is administered by either the designated mediation service provider or conducted by a certified mediator.

sections.label: Mediations excluded from Bill
sections.summary: The Bill will not apply to mediations under the Industrial Relations Act, the Family Justice Court under the Women's Charter, or the Small Claims Tribunal framework.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The Bill will not apply to mediations conducted under the Industrial Relations Act, those conducted by the Family Justice Court under the Women's Charter, or those conducted under the Small Claims Tribunal framework.

sections.label: CMC updates, confidentiality, recording, citation year
sections.summary: CMC will update whether referred parties agreed to mediate and whether mediation resulted in settlement; confidentiality can be waived by consent; recording means written Court order; citation year changes to 2017.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In other words, CMC will update them whether the referred parties have agreed to attempt mediation and, if they do so, whether the mediation materialised in a settlement or otherwise.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: For mediations which are governed by the Bill, as is the case today, confidentiality can be waived if all parties consent to disclosure.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: As regard to the "recording" of a mediated settlement agreement, under clause 12 of the Bill, it refers to recording of the mediated settlement agreement as a Court order, that means, in a written format.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: The citation year "2016" will be changed to "2017", as indicated in the Order Paper Supplement.
